As per learned counsel for the applicant, petitioner is no more as he has died on 01.04.2022.

As per learned counsel for the applicant, he has moved an application for bringing LRs on record,
but same is not available on record.
Matter is pending for more than 10 years.
Therefore, learned counsel for the applicant is heard finally.

This petition has been filed assailing the order dated 27.09.2023, passed in Criminal Revision No.189/2012 (Brajbhushan Prasad Kushwaha Vs.Premlal and Others), whereby learned VII ASJ,
Rewa, Link Court, Mauganj affirmed order dated 19.05.2012, passed by the Court of JMFC, Mauganj whereby learned JMFC discharged respondents from offence under Section 420 of IPC as it found that no prima facie material available on record to frame charges under Section 420 of IPC.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that learned courts below have not properly appreciated the facts and material on record.

sentences.text: It is contended that dispute is regarding entries made in the revenue papers on the basis of partition between the parties.
Deceased petitioner had filed a complaint before the learned JMFC who had registered complaint on the basis of partition deed and decree passed by learned trial Cort.
Learned JMFC had taken cognizance against Premlal and Sundariya for commission of offence under Section 420 of IPC.
The evidence before charge was recorded.

After recording evidence and hearing parties at the stage of framing charge, learned JMFC found that matter is of civil nature and applicant is required to initiate the proceedings for correction of entries in revenue papers.
Therefore, no case for framing charge under Section 420 of IPC is made out.
It is also the finding that case is of civil nature.
Hence, he discharged the accused respondent from commission of offence under Section 420 of IPC.

Against the impugned order, a revision was preferred by the petitioner - Brajbhushan Prasad Kushwaha, same was also dismissed by the learned II ASJ, Rewa vide order 27.09.2013, passed in Criminal Revision No.89/2012.
I have gone through the impugned orders passed by the Courts below.
On a perusal of the evidence of Brajbhushan, it is apparent that dispute was regarding partition of the ancestral property.
The matter was purely of civil nature.

If there was any discrepancy in the revenue record about recording the share of parties, aggrieved party was required to move an application before the revenue authorities to correct the entries made in revenue papers.

Only because some entries made in the revenue papers by the revenue authorities are wrong or have not been properly entered, it cannot be said that respondent/accused have committed any act with a dishonest intention or with a view to defraud the complainant.

On scanning and examining of the impugned order in the light of material available, it is apparent that learned Courts below have not committed any error in discharging the respondent from Brajbhushan Prasad Kushwaha vs Premlal on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65428715/
2 commission of offence under Section 420 of IPC as necessary ingredients to frame charge under Section 420 of IPC are completely missing.
Therefore, no infirmity or illegality is visible in the impugned orders.
Consequently, this petition being devoid of merits is dismissed.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Jasleen Brajbhushan Prasad Kushwaha vs Premlal on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65428715/
